transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. Um, well, I guess I'm here because... I hope I'm not wasting your time, but I just can’t seem to keep my mind on things the way I used to. 

It's probably nothing major, maybe just getting a little older or a bit of stress, but I'll be at work—I'm a credit counselor—and I'll just stare at a loan worksheet or a client follow-up list, and I find myself rereading the same line over and over. And then I kind of... put off making my calls, just because even simple decisions feel a little harder than they should right now. I hope I'm explaining that okay? Is that the kind of thing you need to know?
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things the way you used to, like hobbies or even work tasks that you used to find satisfying?

Well, I... I guess maybe a little? I really try to stay positive, I promise I do, and I don't want to sound like a complainer. But most days lately, there's just this... I don't know, this dull heaviness kind of sitting with me. 

I still go to the community center, and I still get out into my garden—I know how important it is to keep active! But... well, those are places that always used to lift me up, and lately I feel like I’m just going through the motions. I make sure to keep a smile pasted on so I don't bring anyone else down, but it just doesn't feel the same inside. I hope that doesn't sound too awful? I know I have a lot to be thankful for, I really do. Is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or like you’re not good enough for things lately, even if you know logically that doesn’t make sense?

Oh, goodness, um... no, I don't believe so. I mean, I always try to do my very best for my clients at the agency, and for my friends and family. I know I make mistakes sometimes, just like anyone else, but I don't really sit around feeling guilty or... or like I'm not good enough. 

I try very hard to be a good person and pull my own weight, so I don't really have those specific thoughts weighing on me. I hope that's okay to say? I don't want to sound boastful at all, I just haven't really noticed feeling that way. Am I giving you the right kind of information?
Have you noticed feeling fatigued or like you don’t have the same energy lately, even after a good night's rest?

Well, um... I suppose I have been a little more tired than usual. I really hate to admit it, because I know I should have plenty of energy, and I don't want to sound lazy. But lately, even when I get a full, good night's sleep, I wake up and I just feel... well, still tired. 

I try my best to push through it, I promise I do! But by the time I've done just a couple of client calls for work, or... or just gone out and watered the tomatoes, my body feels like I’ve already put in a whole day. It's probably just a normal part of getting older, right? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately, like eating less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Oh, um... no, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, my appetite seems pretty much the same as always. I still make sure to eat my regular meals, and I haven't noticed my clothes fitting any differently or anything like that. 

I try to make sure I'm taking good care of myself and eating right, so... so no, I don't think there have been any changes there. I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right answers.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to think clearly or concentrate lately, like your thoughts feeling slowed down or it being harder to focus on tasks?

Well, um... I really hate to say it, but... yes, I suppose I have. That's actually a big part of why I decided to come in. I don't want you to think I'm losing my touch or not doing a good job for my clients, but... lately, I just can't seem to keep my mind on things the way I used to. 

I'll be looking at a loan worksheet or a follow-up list, and I'll find myself just staring at it. I'll read the same line over and over again, and it just doesn't seem to stick. And then... well, I end up putting off making my calls because even simple little decisions just feel so much harder than they should. I feel terrible about it, I really do. I try so hard to stay focused, but it's just been a bit of a struggle lately. Is that... is that the sort of thing you're looking for? I hope I'm explaining it alright.
Have you felt down, sad, or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Well, um... I really don't want to sound like a complainer, because I know I have so much to be grateful for. But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest, there has been this... this sort of dull heaviness sitting with me most days. 

I try to keep a positive attitude, I really do! I make sure to keep a smile on my face, especially when I'm at the community center or out in my garden. But lately... well, even in those places that usually lift my spirits so much, I just feel like I'm going through the motions. The smile is there, but underneath it, I just feel a bit... flat, I guess. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm unappreciative of my life. I'm just trying to answer your question correctly... does that make sense?
Have you found that you don’t take much pleasure or interest in almost all activities, even ones you used to enjoy?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I really do try to stay active and engaged with things. I mean, I still go to the community center, and I still get out into my garden when the weather is nice. I know how important it is to keep busy.

I suppose... well, maybe I don't get quite the same spark out of them as I used to, but I definitely still have an interest in them. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing all day! I always try to make an effort. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to be sure I'm giving you an accurate picture.
Has it been harder lately to make even small decisions or to organize your thoughts clearly while working on tasks?

Oh, um... yes, I think that's what I was trying to explain a little earlier. I hope it's alright that I brought it up before you asked! I really don't want to confuse things. 

But yes, like I mentioned, that's actually the main reason I finally decided to come in. I just can't seem to keep my mind on things the way I normally do. I'll be sitting there staring at a client follow-up list or a loan worksheet, and I realize I'm just rereading the exact same line over and over. And then... well, I end up putting off making my calls because figuring out what to do next, even the really simple decisions, just feels so much harder than it should right now. I try my absolute best to push through it so my clients don't notice a thing, I really do. Does that... does that help answer what you were asking?
Would you say that you’ve lost interest in most activities, even ones you used to enjoy, like they don’t bring you any pleasure anymore?

Oh, um... I think we might have just talked about that a little bit, didn't we? I hope I didn't answer out of turn before! 

But, um, just to be sure I'm giving you what you need... no, I wouldn't say I've lost interest completely. Like I mentioned, I still make sure to get out to the garden and go to the community center. I really do try to keep up with everything. It's just... maybe the joy isn't quite as bright as it used to be. But I'm definitely still trying! I hope that's alright, that I'm repeating myself a little? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Would you say your fatigue has gotten to the point where it’s noticeably interfering with your ability to get things done, even basic tasks, or do you feel like you're managing okay most of the time?

Oh, well... I try very hard not to let it interfere, I really do. I don't want to be one of those people who just complains about being tired all the time. But... well, I suppose it has been a little difficult lately. 

Even when I get a full night's sleep, I seem to wake up feeling just as tired as when I went to bed. And then... oh, it's a bit embarrassing to admit, but by the time I've just done a couple of client calls for work, or maybe just gone out to water the tomatoes, my body feels like I've already put in a whole twelve-hour day. I really do push myself to keep going, though, so I'm managing as best as I can. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses? I just want to be honest with you about how it's been feeling.
Would you say that activities you used to really enjoy, like gardening or going to the community center, feel completely uninteresting or unmotivating to you now, even though you still do them?

Oh, dear, I feel like I'm making you ask the same things over and over, and I'm so sorry if I wasn't clear enough before! I really don't want to waste your time. 

But, um, to answer your question... no, I wouldn't say they're completely uninteresting. Not at all. I still care very much about my tomatoes, and I love seeing the folks at the center. It's not that I don't want to do those things. It's just... well, maybe it takes a little more effort to get myself out the door than it used to. But once I'm there, I still try my best to be present and enjoy it. I don't want to give the impression that I've just given up on everything, because I promise I haven't. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right this time.
Would you say that you take no pleasure or interest in almost all activities, including those you used to enjoy like gardening or going to the community center?

Oh, goodness, I... I think we're going around in circles a little bit, aren't we? I am so, so sorry if I'm being confusing or not giving you the right kind of answers. I really am trying to be helpful!

But, um, no, it's definitely not that I take *no* pleasure in them. I really do still care. Like I said, I still go out to the garden, and I still check in at the community center. I wouldn't do those things if I didn't care at all, you know? It's just... well, maybe it's just that I'm so tired these days that it's hard to feel that spark as much. But I promise I haven't lost interest completely. I'm still trying my very best to keep my chin up and stay involved. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Would you say that you take no pleasure or interest in almost all activities, including those you used to enjoy like gardening or going to the community center?

Oh, dear... I feel terrible, I must really be making a mess of this for you to have to ask me again. I am so sorry, I feel like I'm wasting your time. I know you're very busy. 

I... I don't think I take *no* pleasure in them. I really don't. I still go out and tend to my tomatoes, and I still go down to the center. I just... I suppose maybe I don't get quite as much joy out of it as I used to, just because I'm so worn out all the time. But I haven't given up, I promise! I still care. I'm really trying not to let things slide. Is... is that what you were asking? I hope I'm not being too difficult.
Would you say that you take absolutely no pleasure or interest in almost all activities, including those you used to enjoy, like gardening or going to the community center?

Oh, my... I am just so incredibly sorry. I must be doing a really terrible job of explaining myself if you're having to ask me this again. I feel awful taking up so much of your time with my rambling, I really do. 

But, um... no. I wouldn't say I take absolutely no pleasure in things. I mean, I'm still out there watering my plants, and I still talk to everyone at the center. I really do try to keep busy and stay positive! It's just... well, it's just a little harder to feel that excitement when I'm feeling so drained, you know? But I certainly haven't lost all interest. I hope I'm making sense this time... I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. Am I doing okay?
Would you say that you experience no interest or pleasure at all in nearly everything, including things you used to enjoy, most days?

Oh, doctor... I... I feel like I'm failing a test here, and I am so, so sorry. You've had to ask me this so many times, and I must just be doing a dreadful job of giving you what you need. I really hate being a bother to you when I know you have so many other patients to see. 

But I... I honestly don't think I've lost all interest in everything. I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is! I still get up, I still go to work and help my clients with their credit counseling, and I still try to find the bright spots in my day. I promise I'm not completely checked out. I'm just a bit... well, maybe just a bit more tired than I ought to be, so the joy is just a little quieter. 

I hope that's an alright answer? I really am trying my best to explain it right for you. Please tell me if I need to explain it differently, I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
